the evolution of single-particle spectra of cadmium isotopes with neutron number from 50 to 86 is analyzed in the framework of dispersive optical model with the parameters extrapolated to the neutron-rich region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of single-particle neutron characteristics in Cd isotopes in the region of N = 50 to 80.
the neutron drip line of nuclei with Z = 48.
the neutron single-particle characteristics of Cd isotopic nuclei with 50 ≤ N ≤ 82.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutron shell structure of Cd isotopes is not a simple superposition of single-particle states of spherical potential, as was suggested earlier.
a neutron shell model is a good approximation for the description of neutron-rich Cd nuclei.
the 174 Cd isotope has a neutron drip line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dispersive optical model is a useful tool for studying the structure and evolution of nuclei in the neutron-deficient and -excess regions.

the dispersive optical model is able to describe the evolution of the single-particle spectra of Cd isotopes in the region of neutron numbers N of 50–82 and to predict the neutron drip line for Cd isotopes.
the dispersive optical model can be successfully applied to the description of the single-particle spectra in the Cd isotopic chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutron excess of Cd isotopes is a good probe for studying the evolution of magic features of the nuclear shell structure.
a dispersive optical potential with a fixed energy dependence is a suitable tool for the analysis of single-particle neutron characteristics in the region of Cd isotopes.
the dispersive optical model can be applied to the description of single-particle neutron characteristics and the structure of unstable nuclei in the region of neutron excess.
